:::{#def-least-squares}
#### Least squares solution

Let $\matr{A}$ be $m \times n$ and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$.
A **least squares solution** of $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$
is a vector $\hat{\vecf{x}} \in \reals^n$ such that

$$
\norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{A} \hat{\vecf{x}}} \le \norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{A} \vecf{x}}
\quad \text{for every } \vecf{x} \in \reals^n.
$$

The equations $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{b}$
are the **normal equations**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-least-squares}
#### Fitting a constant

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\vecf{b} = (1, 3)$.
The system $x\,(1, 1) = (1, 3)$ is inconsistent (@def-consistent-system):
its first entry needs $x = 1$ and its second needs $x = 3$.
For any number $x$,
$\norm{\vecf{b} - \matr{A} x}^2 = (1 - x)^2 + (3 - x)^2 = 2\,(x - 2)^2 + 2$,
which is smallest at $x = 2$, so $\hat{x} = 2$ is the least squares solution.
The value $x = 1$ is not one: it gives $0 + 4 = 4 > 2$.
The normal equations read $2x = 4$, and their solution is $x = 2$ too.

:::
